main_body: Thatched hut: a large hipped thatch roof (rows 4-51) over a log-plank front wall (rows 52-78) with a central framed doorway and two round shields
top_band: Golden thatch roof slope, rows ~5-51 in one pixel column through the middle. It shows horizontal courses with a lighter tone at the top and a lighter eave edge at about rows 49-51. Hip slopes are visible at the left and right edges.
evidence: The roof is a large sloped surface that clearly reads as a top, with a lighter eave course at its bottom edge. A dark shadow band under the eave (rows ~52-56) leads into the log wall. The wall has vertical planks with tinted shading. The door is inset, with a wooden frame, a stone lintel line and a dark interior, and a stone base runs along the bottom. The tapered hip edges at the sides match how the Beodeul house roofs are built, so both the roof surface and the front face are present.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 5 steps (highlight, light, mid, dark course lines, deep shadow), with per-course dashes and highlight clumps at the left edge. The wall planks are shaded in several browns with grain, and the shield discs have rim, center and orange boss. The stone threshold is mottled. Outlines are dark brown and olive, tinted to match the neighbouring material, not black. Tile density is comparable to the references, with no large flat fills. The deep-shadowed door interior is the only simple area.
